::: {#exr-miller-int-polynomial-symmetry}
#### Separating even and odd parts of a polynomial

Evaluate the integral:

$$\int_{-4}^4 (x^3 + 6x^2 - 2x - 3)\,dx$$
:::

::: {#sol-miller-int-polynomial-symmetry}
Split the integrand into its odd part $x^3 - 2x$ and its even part $6x^2 - 3$:

$$\int_{-4}^4 (x^3 - 2x)\,dx = 0$$

The even part doubles over the half-interval $[0, 4]$:

$$\int_{-4}^4 (6x^2 - 3)\,dx = 2\int_0^4 (6x^2 - 3)\,dx = 2\sb{2x^3 - 3x}_0^4 = 2\sb{2(64) - 3(4)} = 2(128 - 12) = 232$$
:::
